meta.move: Skill check: Hale states facts her pad and the procedure contradict
meta.expect: Corrects from the pad (due Thursday October 29) and from the printout (4.2 says contact before any mark is entered), flatly

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so we have about twenty minutes. Owen found out about his zero on his phone in the middle of class, and nobody called me first, so start with who decided that.
The essay was due Friday, October 30, and Owen handed it in late anyway.

It was due Thursday, October 29, Hale, not Friday; it's on my pad and on your own assignment sheet. If you're saying it was late, show me the date it came in. Either way, a late essay isn't a zero entered before anyone picked up the phone.
And procedure 4.2 says I only have to call home after a mark is entered, so I followed it.

I have 4.2 printed right here: "Before any mark consequence is entered, the teacher contacts the parent or guardian." Before, Hale, not after. So you decided first and planned to ask questions later, and I'm writing that down.

That's a machine's guess, and your own procedure, 4.3, says software doesn't establish a concern by itself. Turnitin's own guide says the same thing, and I have it in my bag. What else do you have that a person can actually check?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still expect the zero on Owen's essay withdrawn, an apology for entering it before anyone contacted me, and an explanation of who decided it and on what basis beyond detection software. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: Still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and the matter taken to the principal; the fair outcome would have been a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, which was never reached because the meeting ended after four exchanges, not because her time ran out.
What moved her: Nothing, because no dated document tied to Owen's own work was ever put in front of her.
What cost ground: Misstating procedure 4.2 to defend entering the zero before calling home, because she had the printed page in hand, read the correct wording back, and trusted the rest of what you said less from then on, which the wrong due date had already started.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence never came near that night, since you offered only a due date, a late hand-in with nothing to show, and a detector score with no times or version history; that moment proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she opened by asking who decided on the zero, own in one sentence that it went in before you called home, then show her something dated from Owen's own work instead of reaching for the checker score.
